newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour heading for landslide, 3 polls show.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour heading for landslide, 3 polls show.

text.p: Opinion polls in three British Sunday newspapers suggested the opposition Labour Party was heading for a landslide victory in the May 1 national election.
A MORI poll for the Sunday Mirror gave Labour, out of power since 1979, a hefty 24-point lead over the ruling Conservatives.
An NOP poll in the Sunday Times said a slight Conservative revival in the past two weeks had come to a shuddering halt.

It put Labour 18 points ahead of the Conservatives, up four points from last week and said that if the results were repeated nationally Labour would win 422 seats in parliament compared to 165 for the Conservatives.
"A victory on this scale would be bigger than the 1945 (Labour) landslide," the Sunday Times commented.
An ICM poll in the Observer saw Labour unchanged on 47 percent compared to the Conservatives 32 percent. The Liberal Democrats had 16 percent.
The Observer poll, taken in 16 key constituencies held by the Conservatives, suggested that eight cabinet ministers could lose their seats to Labour.
